title: New satellite images show Europe’s disappearing rivers due to drought
facts: The European Commission's Joint Research Centre reported record-low water levels on the Loire, Po, Rhine, and Danube rivers.
The Combined Drought Indicator showed half of Europe's land area experienced drought conditions in mid-July.
Nine percent of European land reached drought alert status in mid-July.
Satellite imagery from August 8, 2026, revealed expanded sand and gravel banks along the Loire River near Saumur.
The Garonne River management authority initiated water level support operations in early July.
The July water intervention on the Garonne River was the earliest operation launched since 1993.
Satellite images taken near Kaub, Germany, revealed extensive exposed areas in the Rhine River channel.
Low water levels on the Rhine River halted commercial shipping traffic at river bottlenecks.
Satellite imagery showed significant decreases in water coverage along the Po River near Boretto, Italy.
Declining water levels on the Danube River impacted commercial navigation and agriculture in Hungary and Romania.
England recorded 6.5mm of rainfall in July 2026, representing 10% of the historical average.
July 2026 was the driest July in England since official meteorological records began in 1836.
The UK Environment Agency declared that 71.3% of England was officially in drought.
Reservoir storage levels across England fell to 69% capacity in August 2026.
SkySat satellite imagery documented severe vegetation decline in Vienna's Auer-Welsbach Park between July 2025 and July 2026.
